title: Lower endpoint push execution
statement: Fix a natural number $E$, an oracle that assigns a Boolean answer to each of four deciders and each Boolean word, an input Boolean word $x$, and a natural number bound $B$. Let $st$ be a state of the eighteen-register machine, with loop counter $C$, scratch registers $T,Z$, saved-endpoint stack $SE$, target endpoint $V$, phase stack $SP$, and code width $w$. If $C=T=Z=0$, every register is at most $B$, $SE\,2^w+V\le B$, and $2SP\le B$, then the machine starting at the phase-false endpoint-push routine, with register values given by $st$ and no answer recorded, reaches the move routine that transfers the midpoint into $V$, with $SE=SE_{st}2^{w_{st}}+V_{st}$, $V=0$, $SP=2SP_{st}$, the other registers unchanged, and no answer recorded. Every configuration strictly before that endpoint satisfies the guard that the machine’s instruction precondition holds and every register is at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: oracle on four deciders and Boolean words
all initial registers at most B

Fix a natural number $E$, an oracle on four deciders and Boolean-string inputs, an input
string $x$, and a natural-number register bound $B$. Suppose a machine state has
$C=T=Z=0$, all registers at most $B$, the updated endpoint stack satisfies $SE\,2^w+V\le
B$, and $2SP\le B$. Then the machine starting at the phase-false push routine, with this
state and no answer recorded, reaches the move routine that transfers the midpoint into

stack set to $2SP$, with no answer recorded; every visited configuration satisfies the
guard requiring the program’s precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
